## The problem
<!-- 
  Describe the issue you are experiencing here to communicate to the
  maintainers. Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened instead.
-->
When all the devices restart at same time due to a power failure, the router may become availaible later than HA. This cause the asuswrt component to fail and the presence detection obvioulsy stop working. Due to the fact that the component do not retry to start, after some time HA set status "not home" also if not true. 

## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Developer tools -> Info.
-->

- Home Assistant release with the issue: 0.107.7 
- Last working Home Assistant release (if known):  
- Operating environment (Hass.io/Docker/Windows/etc.): Raspbian on Raspberry PI 4 
- Integration causing this issue: asuswrt
- Link to integration documentation on our website: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/asuswrt/ 

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
<!--
  An example configuration that caused the problem for you. Fill this out even
  if it seems unimportant to you. Please be sure to remove personal information
  like passwords, private URLs and other credentials.
-->

```
  host: 192.168.10.1
  username: xxxx
  password: xxxxx

device_tracker:
  - platform: asuswrt
    interval_seconds: 30
    consider_home: 300
```

review_comments: This case, bad credentials, should return False.

We need to be able to distinguish bad credentials from bad connection. Only bad connection should spawn the retry mechanism. Bad credentials should log error and `return False` since it's a non recoverable error.
All errors that are due to user configuring bad config are also non recoverable.
A config flow would help here since we can check the connection during set up and let the user know before finishing the config.

In any case if the user change credential on router the component will fail during startup. In config flow should only asked a limited set of parameters and remaining should be managed in configuration.yaml (for expert use).
I will start to review the code to retry only in case of OSError exception and return false if is_connected report false.

Credentials will normally be part of the config flow, unless they are client secrets in an oauth flow.

If the credentials change we can handle that during set up and launch a new config flow and the user will be notified to complete it again. The only requirement is that we can distinguish bad credentials from bad connection.
Config flow is out of scope for this PR. :+1:

It would be better if we tested the existence of states in the state machine. When there's an error there shouldn't be any states. After the error clears, the setup should complete and states be created. That way we don't rely on the details of our implementation in the tests.
Ok, I will keeep in consideration for next PR. Thx
